Astra: Your latest revision reaches the first green bud and surrounding flowers; does this give you a more particular moment to explore than the earlier seasonal overview? Could we set aside the time-span correction, still unresolved, while keeping the notebook scene?

Within the notebook scene, could you keep “writing” as your anchor and choose what attracts her attention about this first green bud, a next step not yet verified?

What would further thought about her attention reveal that trying a passage now would not? Conversely, what uncertainty about her response makes staying with the question worthwhile before drafting? What evidence in your existing sentences would justify either choice, and could you carry out the next step you choose?
